examples.input: next: `config set brief "Third paragraph is left exactly as it was,   with odd spacing.\n  this line is more indented\n"`

results.1: All six arms: exit 3, and the file is not changed. Only the error wording differs, e.g. `troupe: value would put a more-indented line into a folded scalar`. Some messages name the file path, the offending line or line 2.

context.in_practice: Paragraphs you don't touch are kept exactly, odd spacing included. A paragraph you edit is re-wrapped at the width its old lines had, so a paragraph that used to be short ends up as a tall column of one- or two-word lines. New paragraphs wrap at about 55 columns. If you only reorder paragraphs, five arms re-wrap a moved paragraph and one arm keeps its old line breaks.
context.stakes: When you change one paragraph of a folded `brief: >` text, you want the paragraphs you did not touch to stay byte-for-byte as they were and only the changed text re-wrapped. Otherwise every edit produces a noisy diff, or the wrapping ends up oddly narrow.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: small diffs that keep your existing wrapping, at the cost of very narrow re-wrapping wherever the old paragraph was short.

plan_why: Edits a folded (>) value step by step to show what the shared route does: an unchanged paragraph keeps its odd line breaks and spacing byte for byte; a changed paragraph is re-wrapped at that paragraph's old width; a new paragraph is wrapped at the value's widest old line; reordering paragraphs; a TAB at a likely break point; and a more-indented line, which is refused with exit 3.
routes: Align paragraphs with difflib; unchanged paragraphs keep their bytes; changed ones re-wrap at the old width (default 80)
